0.x: The revolt broke out soon after Dalhousie left (**1856**); his **annexationist policy** caused the great discontent behind it.

1.x: **Awadh annexed Feb 1856** by Dalhousie on the ground of **"misgovernment" (maladministration)**.

Nawab **Wajid Ali Shah** was **dethroned and exiled to Calcutta**; the British accused him of **failing to control the rebellious chiefs and taluqdars** (after the 1801 Subsidiary Alliance he had no army of his own).
He was in fact widely loved; his couplet **"Dar-o-deewar pe hasrat se nazar karte hain, khush raho ahle-watan hum to safar karte hain"** was later sung by revolutionaries.

**Summary Revenue Settlement 1856** – made directly with **village proprietors**; **taluqdars** were **disarmed, forts destroyed**, estates confiscated (taluqdars' share of villages fell from 67% to 38%).
**Bengal Army** sepoys were hurt – Awadh was their home, and their **families bore the new revenue burden**.

r: Bahadur Shah's successors to leave the **Red Fort** (move to the **Qutub, Mehrauli**)
Successors to **lose the imperial title** and be mere **princes**
**Nana Saheb**, adopted son of **Baji Rao II** (last Peshwa)
**Rani Lakshmibai** – adopted son refused the throne
**Begum Hazrat Mahal** – annexation; proclaimed her son **Birjis Qadr** ruler

2.x: The policy of annexation made **Nana Saheb, the Rani of Jhansi and Bahadur Shah** staunch enemies; fear of annexation **turned a sepoy mutiny into a wider revolt**.
**1857 = 100 years after Plassey (1757):** a prophecy said British rule would end on Plassey's centenary (23 June 1857).

3.x: The ruler keeps a **British subsidiary force at his cost**, accepts a **Resident**, and gives up an **independent foreign policy** (no other Europeans in service).
**1800:** the Nizam ceded **Rayalaseema** to pay for the force – the **"Ceded Districts"**.
